title: Typed IDs
description:
Write `struct Id<T>` holding a `u64` and a `PhantomData<T>`:

- `Id::new(n)` and `id.get()`.
- It must be `Copy`, comparable and hashable **whatever `T` is** (so `#[derive]` is not enough: derive adds `T: Copy` and friends as requirements). Implement `Clone`, `Copy`, `PartialEq`, `Eq` and `Hash` by hand.
- `impl Display` prints `#<n>`.

Then write `struct IdGen<T>` with `IdGen::new()` and `next(&mut self) -> Id<T>` giving 1, 2, 3, ...
hints: `#[derive(Clone, Copy)]` on `Id<T>` would only make `Id<T>` copyable when `T` is too. Writing `impl<T> Copy for Id<T> {}` (plus `Clone`) by hand removes that requirement, which is right here because no `T` is ever stored.

The hand-written impls are short. `Clone::clone` can return `*self` once `Copy` is implemented; `Eq` is an empty `impl<T> Eq for Id<T> {}` on top of `PartialEq`. `Hash` has one method, generic over the hasher: `fn hash<H: Hasher>(&self, state: &mut H)`, and its body passes on the fields that matter, here `self.value.hash(state);`.
